introduction_markdown: Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour and Section II in 1 1/2 hours; you are advised to divide your time accordingly. In Section II answer EITHER the a, b and c OR the d, e and f of each question. For your guidance the approximate mark(s) for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Where necessary, assume: the acceleration of free fall, $g = 10\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$; the speed of light in air, $c = 3\times10^{8}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; the charge on an electron, $e = 1.6\times10^{-19}\,\mathrm{C}$. Non-programmable calculators are allowed.

questions.enonce_markdown: State the law of conservation of linear momentum. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown: The **total linear momentum** of a system of interacting (colliding) bodies **remains constant** (is conserved), **provided no external resultant force acts on the system**. In a collision, the total momentum before equals the total momentum after.

questions.enonce_markdown:
A car of mass 2500 kg moving with velocity of $30\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ collides with a stationary car of mass 1500 kg. After collision, the two cars lock together and move with a common velocity.

Calculate:

(i) the total momentum of the system just before collision. *[2 marks]*

(ii) the common velocity with which the locked cars move. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) Momentum of the moving car: $2500\times30 = 75\,000\,\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$. The other car is at rest (momentum $0$).

Total momentum before $= 75\,000 + 0 = 7.5\times10^{4}\,\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$.

(ii) By conservation of momentum, the total after is the same, and the combined mass is $2500 + 1500 = 4000\,\mathrm{kg}$:

$4000\,v = 75\,000$, so $v = \dfrac{75\,000}{4000} = 18.75 \approx 18.8\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$.

**The cars move together at about $18.8\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$.**
